sets.title: Law and method changes
sets.what: Changes since 2016 that break year-to-year comparisons.
rows: Proposal 3 (passed 11/6/2018): no-excuse absentee voting, same-day registration, straight-ticket option restored, automatic registration (Const. art. II s.4)
2016 and 2018 absentee required an excuse (age 60+ etc.): 2016/2018 absentee counts are a different, older electorate and are not like for like with 2020+.
2020 PA 177: one-day (10 hours) pre-processing of absentee envelopes on 11/2/2020 in cities of 25,000+

Proposal 2 (passed 11/8/2022): at least 9 consecutive days of early in-person voting (second Saturday to the Sunday before ED, 8+ hours a day; clerks may add days from the 29th day out); a state-funded drop box per municipality and one per 15,000 voters; single application for a permanent absentee list; photo ID or affidavit; notice and cure of signature defects; UOCAVA ballots postmarked by ED and received within 6 days counted

2022 had no early in-person voting; 2024 was the first general with it. The 2026 absentee-returned series (986,207 at 10/23) EXCLUDES early in-person votes cast from 10/24: label it absentee-only and compare EV with 2024 only.

2023 PA 81 (eff. 2/13/2024): cities/townships of 5,000+ may process AND tabulate absentee ballots 7 a.m.-8 p.m. on any of the 8 days before ED (second Monday through the Monday before); any municipality may do so on the Monday before
2024 and 2026 absentee results can post soon after polls close; 2022 (no pre-ED tabulation [I]) reported later. Affects 'red/blue mirage' timing, not totals.
Absent voter ballots must be received by the clerk by 8 p.m. on ED (UOCAVA exception: postmarked by ED, received within 6 days)
Same receipt rule 2016-2026 for domestic mail.
Agee v. Benson (W.D. Mich., Dec 2023) ordered 13 Detroit-area state legislative districts redrawn; remedial House map used in 2024; Senate seats on the remedial map first elected 2026 [I]
MI Senate district comparisons with 2022 are broken in metro Detroit; congressional map unchanged since 2022.

An anti-voting lawsuit challenging Ingham County, Michigan’s appointment of poll workers.

An anti-voting lawsuit seeking to force Michigan to place a proposed constitutional amendment requiring proof of citizenship to vote on the November 2026 ballot.
The U.S. Supreme Court denied ACVM’s application. The Michigan Supreme Court also denied ACVM’s request for relief.
